chunks: If you ask them: 'Who sends down rain from the sky and quickens the earth when it is dead?' They will answer: 'God.' Say: 'All praise be to God.' But most of them do not understand.

key_terms.مَوْتِهَا: its death (referring to the earth's barrenness)

ai.seo_question: Why do polytheists acknowledge God as the sender of rain but still associate partners with Him?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the cognitive dissonance of polytheists who recognize Allah’s power in natural phenomena like rain yet fail to apply that same monotheistic logic to His sovereignty. It serves as a critique of superficial faith, emphasizing that true 'understanding' (aql) requires moving beyond mere acknowledgment of divine power to exclusive worship. This aligns with the concept of *Tawhid* as both an intellectual realization and a practical commitment.
